programme.desc: Në këtë cikël dokumentar do të ekzaminojmë disa prej Amerikanëve të ashtuquajtur ’të fortë’ dhe do të rendisim cilësitë e tyre të jashtëzakonshme për të zbuluar se cili është më i forti. Ana emocionuese, e parrëfyer dhe tejet mbresëlënëse e ikonave amerikane...

programme.title: Në hijen e Hënës
programme.desc: Një oficer policie me ambicie për t’u bërë detektiv, vihet në gjurmët e një vrasëseje seriale që shfaqet çdo 9 vjet. Kur krimet e saj fillojnë të sfidojnë çdo shpjegim shkencor, fiksimi i tij për të vërtetën kërcënon t’i shkatërrojë karrierën, familjen dhe arsyen.

programme.title: Në gjueti të nazistëve: Gjyqi i Nurembergut
programme.desc: ep. 2, Dokumentar, Pas përfundimit të Luftës së Dytë Botërore, një histori e errët nisi të shkruhej në hije. Kriminelët nazistë, përgjegjës për mizori të papara, nuk u zhdukën, ata u fshehën. Si kundërpërgjigje bota nisi një gjueti pa mëshirë. Nga cikli dokumentar”Nazistët në Arrati”, vjen një zbërthim i detajuar i rrjetit sekret të largimeve e arratisjeve për t’i shpëtuar gjykimit

Por në vitin 2015, diçka e tmerrshme ndodhi. Pas aksidentit, numri i vizitorëve ra. Si ja arritën ideatorët e parkut, të tërheqin përsëri vizitorët?

Inteligjenca Artificiale po zhvillohet me ritme të shpejta, sidomos në industrinë ushtarake. Por a rrezikon IA të dalë jashtë kontrollit, të Inteligjencës njerëzore?!

programme.desc: Si po ndërton ditë pas dite planeti ynë, një sistem nervor ku secili prej nesh funksionon si një sensor njerëzor. Si përcojmë në cdo moment informacion se ku jetojmë, ku shkojmë, ç’blejmë, ç’themi. Por si po na shërben ne, ky oqean të dhënash?

programme.title: Të krijosh nga plehrat
programme.desc: Kris Haket, një Artist dhe Krijues... Për të, nuk ka rëndësi se ku jeton, mjafton të jetë i lirë, për të bërë Artin e tij... Art, të cilin e krijon me mbeturinat... Po po, ato që ju hidhni... Mësoni dhe ju prej Kris Haket...

programme.desc: Ndërtesat shekullore kanë mahnitur shkencëtarët për shek. me radhë. Sot, teknologjia më e re, mund t’i eksplorojë këto struktura në një mënyrë që syri njerëzor s’e bën dot. Një udhëtim pas në kohë, për të kuptuar misteret më të vjetra të inxhinierisë

programme.title: Gjuajtja perfekte
programme.desc: Një cikël interesant për të gjithë të apasionuarit pas armëve ku qitës të specialiteteve të ndryshme që do të rivalizojnë si në skuadra ashtu edhe individualisht me armë moderne dhe të vjetra e ku çdo javë do të eleminohet një qitës.

programme.title: Mjekësia magjike 2
programme.desc: Një ekip studiuesish britanikë vendosin të trajtojnë me kërpudha magjike 20 personave që vuajnë nga depresioni i rëndë... Le të zbulojmë sëbashku rezultatet e këtij eksperimenti që u dehsën 3 vjet për të marrë rezultatet.

programme.title: Mjekësia magjike 2
programme.desc: Një ekip studiuesish britanikë vendosin të trajtojnë me kërpudha magjike 20 personave që vuajnë nga depresioni i rëndë... Le të zbulojmë sëbashku rezultatet e këtij eksperimenti që u dehsën 3 vjet për të marrë rezultatet.

programme.title: Perspektiva aliene
programme.desc: Një udhëtim drejt të panjohurës. Le të zbulojmë së bashku shenjat dhe përvojat e jetës jashtë tokës. Pamje të rralla, intervista dhe analiza shkencore, që do të sfidojnë perceptimet tona për universin.

programme.title: Projektet sekrete të UFO-ve 2
programme.desc: 75 vjet më parë, një skuadron me avionë gjuajtës të Shteteve të Bashkuara, vëzhgoi objekte fluturuese të paidentifikuara lart në kufirin franko-gjerman gjatë Luftës së II Botërore. Megjithëse pretendimet për takime jashtëtokësore janë hedhur poshtë, shumë besojnë se ekzistenca e UFO-ve nuk është thjesht e mundshme, por e sigurt...

programme.title: Mjekësia ligjore ekstreme
programme.desc: Skena krimi dhe mendje kriminale aq të çuditshme sa nuk mund t’i shpjegosh. Për të shkuar tek e vërteta, duhen Ekspertizat Ekstreme. Raste kriminale, që kanë shokuar opinionin dhe kanë spikatur në karrierën e detektivëve më të famshëm.

programme.title: Universi ekstrem
programme.desc: Për mijëra vite kemi pyetur a është Toka planeti i vetëm me jetë, në këtë kozmos të pafundmë?Apo jemi pjesë e diçkaje më të madhe? Cilat janë teknologjitë e reja për të kërkuar dhe ndoshta për të komunikuar me qytetërime të përparuara jashtëtokësorës

programme.title: Prototipi
programme.desc: Një grup shpikësish, të izoluar në një magazinë në San Francisko, duhet të projektojnë, realizojnë dhe të na prezantojnë prototipat e të ardhmes, të cilët janë të llojeve, përmasave dhe funksioneve të ndryshme ...

programme.title: Historia e shkrimit Helvetika
programme.desc: Ai është formati i të shkruarit më i përdorur në Botë. Si dhe kur lindi shkrimi Helvetika? Pse u konsiderua si një arritje e dizanjit grafik ?

programme.title: Historia e shkrimit Helvetika
programme.desc: Ai është formati i të shkruarit më i përdorur në Botë. Si dhe kur lindi shkrimi Helvetika? Pse u konsiderua si një arritje e dizanjit grafik ?

programme.title: Taksia ekologjike
programme.desc: Luis Palmeri ka vendosur të shëtisë botën me një makinë shumë të veçantë, që vihet në punë me energji diellore. Ai do të udhëtojë drejt 40 shteteve, për 1 vit e gjysëm dhe kështu të vërtetojë se udhëtimi me energji diellore është i mundur.

programme.title: Spiunët kozmik
programme.desc: Historia e astrospiunëve... Si dhe pse u morr vendimi për të lëshuar në hapësirë satelitë spiunë... Cfarë ndodhi gjatë Luftës së ftohtë dhe cili ishte sateliti i parë që arriti të fotografonte prej lartësisë 160 km mbi Tokë...

programme.title: Barka që ndërtoi Gai
programme.desc: Ai është një njeri me një pasion shumë të madh. Gai Martin, çiklist i famshëm botëror dhe mekanik kamionësh, do të transforjmojë një barkë të shkatërruar, në krenarinë e shpikjeve të mëdha të Britanikëve të Revolucionit Industrial.

programme.title: Gjuajtja perfekte

programme.title: Efekti i Instagramit
programme.desc: Në pak më shumë se 10 vjet, Instagrami është kthyer në një ndër kompanitë më me ndikim të medias sociale në botë. Instagram ka fituar mbi një miliard përdorues, duke ndikuar në kulturën, tendencat dhe mënyrën se si njerëzit jetojnë jetën e tyre. Por ndikimi i Instagramit në shoqër, po vihet gjithnjë e më shumë në pikëpyetje, ndërsa qeveritë po bëjnë përpjekje për kontrolluar mediat sociale.

programme.title: Projektet sekrete të UFO-ve 4

Megjithëse pretendimet për takime jashtëtokësore janë hedhur poshtë, shumë besojnë se ekzistenca e UFO-ve nuk është thjesht e mundshme, por e sigurt...

programme.title: A mund të jetojmë përgjithmonë

programme.title: Aksidenti ajror më i rëndë në histori

Një program çdo të hënë dhe të enjte në prime time, ku diskutohen temat më te nxehta të politikës, analizë, debate dhe komente, intervista me personalitetet më të rëndësishme të politikës, ekonomisë, historisë, kulturës etj. Emisioni Drejt sjell të gjitha këndvështrimet e ngjarjeve në vend, rajon dhe më gjerë.

Nën drejtimin e moderators Sonila Musaj, nuk do të mungojnë ekspertët dhe analistët e duhur për të dhënë opinionin e tyre, por as njerëzit e thjeshtë që preken nga vendimmarrjet e gabuara dhe padrejtësitë.

programme.title: Ora E Betit
programme.desc: Një emision nga gazetarja Beti Njuma. Transmetohet çdo të marte dhe të mërkurë ora 20:45 në RTV Ora. Nje emision i aktualitetit i fokusuar tek Shqipëria dhe Kosova, duke i parë ato si një hapësirë e vetme, pranë dhe larg njëra tjetrës. Të ftuarit dhe debati do na ndihmojnë me refleksionet e tyre, për të kuptuar dritëhijet e një vendi kontradiktor, në zgrip dhe prej 31 vitesh me sytë nga Europa.

programme.title: D-Night
programme.desc: Emisioni ”D-Night Show”, nga Dajana Shabani, rikthehet edhe këtë sezon! Argëtues, satirik, një show i vërtetë kur protagonistë bëhen dhe vetë shqiptarët me komentet e tyre. Kësaj here me një tjetër personazh. ”D-Night” sjell realitetin shqiptar në formë ironike. Të ftuar në studio, histori të jetuara, lidhje skype, kohë viralësh e shumë të tjera në shoën që argëton shqiptarët

programme.title: Përbindëshat e Kutive
programme.desc: Poshtë rrugëve të një qyteze, jetojnë disa krijesa të quajtura ’përbindëshat e kutive’. Kur ata këcënohen nga një njeri shpirtkeq,Veza, djali që ata kanë rritur, do të dalë në rrugët e qytetit që të shpëtojë familjen e tij të pazakontë...

programme.title: Shpata në gur
programme.desc: Anglia ish e lire kur ne krye kishte nje mbret te mire. Nje dite mbreti vdiq dhe froni i arte ngeli bosh. Duhej gjetur nje trashegimtar djale trim dhe luftetar. Kushdo qe shpaten do ta nxirrte nga guri do te behej mbret i Anglise.

programme.title: Princesha dhe pasqyra magjike
programme.desc: Në një vend të magjishëm, Tomi i vogël por me guxim të madh, do të nis një rrugëtim për të çliruar vendin e tij nga magjia dhe për të fituar zemrën e priceshës së bukur...

programme.title: Ponio
programme.desc: Djaloshi Soske, gjen një peshk me emrin Ponio, që ka aftësinë të kthehet në njeri. Soske dhe Ponio, nisin një udhëtim fantastik miqësie dhe eksplorimi. Por Ponio duhet të zgjedhë: të qëndrojë peshk apo të kthehet përgjithmonë në njeri?

programme.title: Bota e re

programme.title: Qielli i saj i kaltër
programme.desc: Pas humbjes së prindërve, Akane fillon të kujdeset për motrën e vogël Aoi, madje për të, ajo refuzon ftesën e shokut të saj Shinosuke për tu shkolluar në Tokio. Por pas 13 vitesh nga takimi i tyre i fundit, ai rikthehet në rrethana shumë misterioze...

programme.title: Përbindëshi im i ëmbël
programme.desc: Princeshë Barbara arratiset nga palati mbretëror sepse nuk do të martohet me postierin i cili do vetëm pushtet....Por Bugi, një përbindësh shumë i ëmbël, e ndihmon Barbarën të rikthehet që të shpëtojë mbretërinë e saj...

programme.title: Qeni rokstar 2: Në park ka një festë
programme.desc: Kur kitarristi i talentuar Bodi dhe grupi i tij, largohen nga Mali me dëborë për të shoqëruar në turne yllin e pop-it, dhelprën Lil’, ata do të mësojnë se Fama, e ka gjithmon një çmim...

programme.title: Mbretëreria e dëborës

programme.desc: Marina, një sirenë e vetmuar, është mërzitur me jetën nën ujë. Dëshira e saj më e madhe është që të ketë këmbë. Një ditë ajo shkon tek shtriga e ujit e cila i jep një bilbil magjik që sa herë i fryn të kthen në njeri ose sirenë.

programme.title: Aventurat e sirenës së vogël
programme.desc: Marina, një sirenë e vetmuar, është mërzitur me jetën nën ujë. Dëshira e saj më e madhe është që të ketë këmbë. Një ditë ajo shkon tek shtriga e ujit e cila i jep një bilbil magjik që sa herë i fryn të kthen në njeri ose sirenë.

programme.title: Bleteza Xhulia
programme.desc: Kjo eshte nje histori e nje bleteze qe fluturon e qete duke shijuar jeten. Por ajo donte te bente nje jete me dinjitoze dhe te kishte emrin Xhulia. Per kete, Bleteza punetore shkon te pyesi nenen mbretereshe.

programme.title: Mbretëria e Rodencias dhe dhëmbi i princeshës
programme.desc: Në mbretërinë përrallore të Rodensias, miushët Edam dhe Bri duhet të zbulojnë me çdo kusht magjinë e dhëmbit të princeshës për të mbrojtur mbretërinë e tyre nga armiqtë që e kërcënojnë atë.

programme.title: Kënga e detit
programme.desc: Kjo është aventura e merkullueshme e Benit dhe motrës së tij më të vogël Sirsha, e cila mund të kthehet në një fokë deti... Një film emocionues që nuk duhet humbur...

programme.title: Filmi i Planktonit
programme.desc: Planktoni ka një histori të ndërlikuar dashurie me një kompjuter dhe çdo gjë shkon shumë keq kur ajo vendos të shkaterrojë botën, pa të. Kjo ishte ideja Planktonit si fillim dhe tani ai duhet që më parë ta shpëtojë botën dhe pastaj të vendosë çfarë do të bëjë.

programme.title: Bleteza Xhulia

programme.title: Barni Ylli i Krishtlindjes se Barnit
programme.desc: Barni, nje kukull e vogel transformohet nga imagjinata e femijeve ne nje personazh shume interesant. Ai u meson femijeve kenge dhe lojra.

programme.title: Eksodi i Tokës
programme.desc: If Earth became uninhabitable, where would humans live? In Exodus Earth, the six-part series anchoring SPACE WEEK, physicist and host Dr. Basil Singer eagerly plays the role of human guinea pig to find answers. His mission is to investigate if humans could possibly call Mercury, Venus, Mars, Saturn’s moon Titan, and Jupiter’s moons Callisto and Gliese 581c home in the future. In the name of science, Dr. Singer subjects himself to extreme temperatures; tests new survival technologies designed to keep humans alive in harsh environments; suffers the rigors of travel in zero gravity; explores ideas for new human habitats in the sky; and more.

programme.title: Eksodi i Tokës
programme.desc: If Earth became uninhabitable, where would humans live? In Exodus Earth, the six-part series anchoring SPACE WEEK, physicist and host Dr. Basil Singer eagerly plays the role of human guinea pig to find answers. His mission is to investigate if humans could possibly call Mercury, Venus, Mars, Saturn’s moon Titan, and Jupiter’s moons Callisto and Gliese 581c home in the future. In the name of science, Dr. Singer subjects himself to extreme temperatures; tests new survival technologies designed to keep humans alive in harsh environments; suffers the rigors of travel in zero gravity; explores ideas for new human habitats in the sky; and more.

programme.title: In and Out
programme.desc: Të rejat nga showbizi, intervista pse jo edhe thashetheme të gjitha këto tashmë do të vijnë përmes emisionit më të ri që ka nisur transmetimin në RTV21 , “In and Out”, nën udhëheqjen e Granit Miftarit. Të mërkurën të enjten dhe të premten duke filluar nga ora 19: 30, Graniti do të jetë pranë jush për të dhënë më të rejat rreth personaliteteve të njohura, qoftë për karrierën e tyre e edhe për jetën private. Në edicionin e parë që u transmetua mbrëmë, mysafir i parë ishtë këngëtarja, Vesa Smolica e cila foli për pjesëmarrjen e saj në festivalin “Kënga Magjike”.

programme.title: In and Out
programme.desc: Të rejat nga showbizi, intervista pse jo edhe thashetheme të gjitha këto tashmë do të vijnë përmes emisionit më të ri që ka nisur transmetimin në RTV21 , “In and Out”, nën udhëheqjen e Granit Miftarit. Të mërkurën të enjten dhe të premten duke filluar nga ora 19: 30, Graniti do të jetë pranë jush për të dhënë më të rejat rreth personaliteteve të njohura, qoftë për karrierën e tyre e edhe për jetën private. Në edicionin e parë që u transmetua mbrëmë, mysafir i parë ishtë këngëtarja, Vesa Smolica e cila foli për pjesëmarrjen e saj në festivalin “Kënga Magjike”.

programme.title: Hitler’s Gold
programme.desc: Munich, September the 12th, 1919. History is about to be changed by a penniless army corporal thirsty to avenge his adoptive motherland. 13 years later, he will be saluted as the savior of the German nation. His name is Adolf Hitler.

programme.title: Hitler’s Gold
programme.desc: Germany, 1937. By imposing his national economic policies by brute force, Adolf Hitler appears to be fulfilling his promise of returning Germany to prosperity within only 4 years. But there was an altogether more sinister side to this economic recovery and even as Germany was basking in the glow of her newfound confidence, Hitler and his cronies were selling her soul. In this episode, we reveal how the Nazis took absolute power over Germany with the financial backing of its industrial elite, and how Hitler would repay them by commissioning them the rearmament of the country, financed by an ingenious credit scheme created by financial wizard Hjalmar Schacht. We reveal how Gustav Krupp von Bohlen became the main industrial figure in the country, along with his financial contributions to the Führer, who himself made a fortune with his own publishing house and royalties. And finally, we reveal how Herman Göering’s plans for autarky would make way for Flick’s and IG Farben’s domination of the Reich economy, but at the same time, lead the country to the verge of economic collapse, and the need for expansion that would inevitably cause the deadliest conflict in the history of mankind.

programme.title: Massive Engineering Mistakes

programme.title: Mysteries of Ancient Medicine

programme.title: How the Tudors Lost Their Heads
programme.desc: Executed on charges of adultery and treason, Anne Boleyn is often remembered as the ‘harlot’ who seduced Henry VIII into annulling his first marriage and forcing his country into religious turmoil. Suzannah Lipscomb and Dan Snow explore evidence that reveals a different Anne, whose ideas transformed England and whose reputation deserves reassessing.

programme.title: How the Tudors Lost Their Heads

But just twelve years on, he was executed for leading a rebellion. Suzannah Lipscomb and Dan Snow unpack Essex’s rapid rise and fall, and the court politics that sealed his fate.

programme.title: Hitler’s Gold
programme.desc: With the help of large corporations inside and outside of Germany, Adolf Hitler has conquered almost half of Europe in less than 4 years. Neutral countries would not only turn a blind eye to the looting but would even become complicit in the crime. Millions would be enslaved for the growth of the Nazi war machine. Even the bodies of their victims would be turned into profit. But in the end, what was it all for? In this episode, we reveal the nature of the American businesses’ dealings with the Third Reich, and how some of America’s more famous corporations would give a definitive contribution to the German war effort, leading to a press scandal that shocked the US. We reveal how the Nazis conquered almost half of Europe, plundering the national money reserves, industries, and cultural treasures of the countries they occupied, including the labor force that would help build its beylic machine, produced by private corporations that willingly financed and supported the Nazi regime. And even after the US entered the war, there were less scrupulous American companies who would keep dealing with the Reich, often using neutral countries as intermediaries. But more than the business of war, there was also the profiting from death, and the massive fortune stolen from the victims of the Holocaust will also not be forgotten.

programme.title: Hitler’s Gold
programme.desc: With the end of the Second World War in Europe, the hunt for Nazi criminals started, along with the wish to bring justice to their victims, including the restitution of stolen goods, property, and possessions during Adolf Hitler’s 12-year reign of terror. While most of it would be recovered, a lot is still missing, leading to several conspiracy theories and treasure hunts. Was part of this loot used to finance the escape networks for Nazi fugitives? Did the Nuremberg trials and other Denazification courts properly punish those who supported Hitler financially and helped him build his deadly war machine? What happened to them after they were released from prison? And did the victims of Nazism and their families recover their stolen assets? Was justice ever served for them? In this episode, we try to answer these questions and more regarding the aftermath and injustice after the rise and fall of one of the deadliest regimes humanity has ever witnessed.

programme.title: Better Than Four
programme.desc: Initially a bi-weekly (26×26’) sports series with a difference, ‘Better Than Four’ brings viewers all the action from all things two-wheeled. As well as profiling past, present and future heroes of cycling, ‘Better Than Four’ includes news features and highlights from the very latest events. Each episode is also packed with tips and tricks to try at home, as well as reviews of the latest kit, equipment and cycling films. Changing gears from traditional cycling coverage, ‘Better Than Four’ takes viewers to new, exotic locations, from the volcano bike-ride in Bali to jungle biking around the Mayan temples of South America. Each episode will include up to 3 segments covering cycling and biking events from all over the world. With amazing footage and commentary from experienced cyclists, daredevil skills and awe-inspiring camerawork, this groundbreaking show is a must for cycling enthusiasts and novices alike.

programme.title: Cape Epic 2019
programme.desc: The Absa Cape Epic is the world’s premier mountain bike stage race. The route changes every year, leading aspiring amateur and professional mountain bikers from around the world through roughly 700km of unspoilt scenery and 15 000m of accumulated climbing, over some of the most magnificent mountain passes in Western Cape in South Africa. The Absa Cape Epic is the most televised mountain bike stage race in the world and the only eight-day mountain bike stage race classed as hors catégorie by the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI). This official UCI status makes it a highlight on the professional racer’s calendar. The Absa Cape Epic also attracts aspiring amateur riders wanting to test themselves against the best. It is a full-service race, meaning that everything is taken care of from the start - all riders need to think about is riding.

programme.title: Cape Epic 2019
programme.desc: The Absa Cape Epic is the world’s premier mountain bike stage race. The route changes every year, leading aspiring amateur and professional mountain bikers from around the world through roughly 700km of unspoilt scenery and 15 000m of accumulated climbing, over some of the most magnificent mountain passes in Western Cape in South Africa. The Absa Cape Epic is the most televised mountain bike stage race in the world and the only eight-day mountain bike stage race classed as hors catégorie by the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI). This official UCI status makes it a highlight on the professional racer’s calendar. The Absa Cape Epic also attracts aspiring amateur riders wanting to test themselves against the best. It is a full-service race, meaning that everything is taken care of from the start - all riders need to think about is riding.

programme.desc: XTERRA is the world’s premier off-road multisport event. An extreme competition, the XTERRA format combines swimming with mountain biking and trail running. programme.title: Cape Epic 2019
programme.desc: The Absa Cape Epic is the world’s premier mountain bike stage race. The route changes every year, leading aspiring amateur and professional mountain bikers from around the world through roughly 700km of unspoilt scenery and 15 000m of accumulated climbing, over some of the most magnificent mountain passes in Western Cape in South Africa. The Absa Cape Epic is the most televised mountain bike stage race in the world and the only eight-day mountain bike stage race classed as hors catégorie by the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI). This official UCI status makes it a highlight on the professional racer’s calendar. The Absa Cape Epic also attracts aspiring amateur riders wanting to test themselves against the best. It is a full-service race, meaning that everything is taken care of from the start - all riders need to think about is riding.

programme.title: Better Than Four
programme.desc: Initially a bi-weekly (26×26’) sports series with a difference, ‘Better Than Four’ brings viewers all the action from all things two-wheeled. As well as profiling past, present and future heroes of cycling, ‘Better Than Four’ includes news features and highlights from the very latest events. Each episode is also packed with tips and tricks to try at home, as well as reviews of the latest kit, equipment and cycling films. Changing gears from traditional cycling coverage, ‘Better Than Four’ takes viewers to new, exotic locations, from the volcano bike-ride in Bali to jungle biking around the Mayan temples of South America. Each episode will include up to 3 segments covering cycling and biking events from all over the world. With amazing footage and commentary from experienced cyclists, daredevil skills and awe-inspiring camerawork, this groundbreaking show is a must for cycling enthusiasts and novices alike.

programme.title: Paragliding World Cup
programme.desc: Superfinalja e Kupës së Botës në Paragliding u zhvillua në Roldanillo, Kolumbi, me dhjetë ditë fluturime konkurruese në nivel të lartë në një nga vendet më të mira të paraglidingut në botë. Njëqind e njëzet e dy pilotë morën pjesë, përfshirë 18 fitues të mëparshëm të përgjithshëm të Kupës së Botës dhe 12 fituese të Kupës së Botës për Femra, duke e renditur atë si një nga garat më të vështira që janë përballur ndonjëherë me njëri-tjetrin. Të pezulluar në ajër, ky sport aventurier përfshin gara në distanca të gjata, ku pilotët duhet të jenë ekspertë në kuptimin e ndikimit të terrenit në kushtet e motit.

programme.title: Andalucia Bike Race 2019
programme.desc: Gara andaluze e biçikletave është gara kryesore e biçikletave malore në Spanjë, e cila përbëhet nga gjashtë etapa dhe zgjat gjashtë ditë. Ritmi i garës nuk bie asnjë minutë gjatë këtyre gjashtë etapave. Në provën e fundit, çiklistët ngjiten në 1396 metra lartësi në mitikun Reventon dhe kalojnë përmes Trassierra-s, pastaj zbresin dhe përfundojnë në itinerarin e paharrueshëm Santo-Domingo. Një gabim në shtigjet shkëmbore do të thotë fundi i garës. Fituesit e edicionit të 9-të ishin spanjolli David Valero në garën e meshkujve dhe norvegjezja Hildegunn Hovdenak në atë të femrave.

programme.title: Cape Epic 2019
programme.desc: The Absa Cape Epic is the world’s premier mountain bike stage race. The route changes every year, leading aspiring amateur and professional mountain bikers from around the world through roughly 700km of unspoilt scenery and 15 000m of accumulated climbing, over some of the most magnificent mountain passes in Western Cape in South Africa. The Absa Cape Epic is the most televised mountain bike stage race in the world and the only eight-day mountain bike stage race classed as hors catégorie by the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI). This official UCI status makes it a highlight on the professional racer’s calendar. The Absa Cape Epic also attracts aspiring amateur riders wanting to test themselves against the best. It is a full-service race, meaning that everything is taken care of from the start - all riders need to think about is riding.

programme.title: CAPE EPIC 2022
programme.desc: The Absa Cape Epic is the world’s premier mountain bike stage race. The route changes every year, leading aspiring amateur and professional mountain bikers from around the world through roughly 700km of unspoilt scenery and 15 000m of accumulated climbing, over some of the most magnificent mountain passes in Western Cape in South Africa. The Absa Cape Epic is the most televised mountain bike stage race in the world and the only eight-day mountain bike stage race classed as hors catégorie by the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI). This official UCI status makes it a highlight on the professional racer’s calendar. The Absa Cape Epic also attracts aspiring amateur riders wanting to test themselves against the best. It is a full-service race, meaning that everything is taken care of from the start - all riders need to think about is riding.

programme.title: Better Than Four
programme.desc: Initially a bi-weekly (26×26’) sports series with a difference, ‘Better Than Four’ brings viewers all the action from all things two-wheeled. As well as profiling past, present and future heroes of cycling, ‘Better Than Four’ includes news features and highlights from the very latest events. Each episode is also packed with tips and tricks to try at home, as well as reviews of the latest kit, equipment and cycling films. Changing gears from traditional cycling coverage, ‘Better Than Four’ takes viewers to new, exotic locations, from the volcano bike-ride in Bali to jungle biking around the Mayan temples of South America. Each episode will include up to 3 segments covering cycling and biking events from all over the world. With amazing footage and commentary from experienced cyclists, daredevil skills and awe-inspiring camerawork, this groundbreaking show is a must for cycling enthusiasts and novices alike.

programme.title: FREERIDE WORLD TOUR 2018
programme.desc: The Freeride World Tour (FWT) expands to Asia! The season kick-off of the world’s most important freeride series for skiers and snowboarders will be held at Hakuba (JPN), the first time ever the FWT stops in the Far East. The second stage of the tour will also guest at a new location, champagne powder paradise Kicking Horse near Golden, British Columbia (CAN). The series continues with the well-proven spectacular slopes of Vallnord-Arcalís (AND), Fieberbrunn (AUT), and Verbier (SUI).

programme.title: Cape Epic 2019
programme.desc: The Absa Cape Epic is the world’s premier mountain bike stage race. The route changes every year, leading aspiring amateur and professional mountain bikers from around the world through roughly 700km of unspoilt scenery and 15 000m of accumulated climbing, over some of the most magnificent mountain passes in Western Cape in South Africa. The Absa Cape Epic is the most televised mountain bike stage race in the world and the only eight-day mountain bike stage race classed as hors catégorie by the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI). This official UCI status makes it a highlight on the professional racer’s calendar. The Absa Cape Epic also attracts aspiring amateur riders wanting to test themselves against the best. It is a full-service race, meaning that everything is taken care of from the start - all riders need to think about is riding.

programme.title: Better Than Four
programme.desc: Initially a bi-weekly (26×26’) sports series with a difference, ‘Better Than Four’ brings viewers all the action from all things two-wheeled. As well as profiling past, present and future heroes of cycling, ‘Better Than Four’ includes news features and highlights from the very latest events. Each episode is also packed with tips and tricks to try at home, as well as reviews of the latest kit, equipment and cycling films. Changing gears from traditional cycling coverage, ‘Better Than Four’ takes viewers to new, exotic locations, from the volcano bike-ride in Bali to jungle biking around the Mayan temples of South America. Each episode will include up to 3 segments covering cycling and biking events from all over the world. With amazing footage and commentary from experienced cyclists, daredevil skills and awe-inspiring camerawork, this groundbreaking show is a must for cycling enthusiasts and novices alike.

programme.title: Xterra Adventures
programme.desc: XTERRA is the world’s premier off-road multisport event. An extreme competition, the XTERRA format combines swimming with mountain biking and trail running. It has been described as one part triathlon, one part mountain bike race, and one part “survival of the fittest”. The typical distances are a 1.5k swim, 30k mountain bike, and 10k trail run.

Every episode Sandy and Daniel enter different events and wholeheartedly get into the spirit of that form of racing.

programme.title: Cape Epic 2019
programme.desc: The Absa Cape Epic is the world’s premier mountain bike stage race. The route changes every year, leading aspiring amateur and professional mountain bikers from around the world through roughly 700km of unspoilt scenery and 15 000m of accumulated climbing, over some of the most magnificent mountain passes in Western Cape in South Africa. The Absa Cape Epic is the most televised mountain bike stage race in the world and the only eight-day mountain bike stage race classed as hors catégorie by the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI). This official UCI status makes it a highlight on the professional racer’s calendar. The Absa Cape Epic also attracts aspiring amateur riders wanting to test themselves against the best. It is a full-service race, meaning that everything is taken care of from the start - all riders need to think about is riding.

programme.title: 4 Deserts Race
programme.desc: Welcome to the world of the 4 Deserts Race Series, the only international ultramarathon series which mixes local culture with trail running. The 4 Deserts Race Series is widely recognized as one of the most prestigious outdoor running series in the world. It is made up of 4 of the most iconic and toughest races in the world - the Sahara Race in Egypt and Namibia, the Gobi March between China and Mongolia, the Atacama Crossing in Chile and The Last Desert in Antarctica. Competitors traverse 250 kilometers in seven days over rough country terrain with only a place in a tent and water provided and support from the very best operational and medical teams provided. Through this documentary, we will travel to two destinations of the 2017 4 Deserts race calendar; China for the Gobi March in the great Gobi Desert and Chile for the Atacama Crossing in the Atacama Desert, an area of extraordinary beauty and astounding natural wonders.

programme.title: The Outdoor Sports Show

From marathon races to climbing, skiing to surfing, hiking to triathlon, sailing to cycling - human meets nature on a thrilling journey of performance.

programme.title: Better Than Four
programme.desc: Initially a bi-weekly (26×26’) sports series with a difference, ‘Better Than Four’ brings viewers all the action from all things two-wheeled. As well as profiling past, present and future heroes of cycling, ‘Better Than Four’ includes news features and highlights from the very latest events. Each episode is also packed with tips and tricks to try at home, as well as reviews of the latest kit, equipment and cycling films. Changing gears from traditional cycling coverage, ‘Better Than Four’ takes viewers to new, exotic locations, from the volcano bike-ride in Bali to jungle biking around the Mayan temples of South America. Each episode will include up to 3 segments covering cycling and biking events from all over the world. With amazing footage and commentary from experienced cyclists, daredevil skills and awe-inspiring camerawork, this groundbreaking show is a must for cycling enthusiasts and novices alike.

programme.title: Audi Winter Games
programme.desc: Stunning scenery, world’s best talent and Kiwi hospitality is set to be showcased to a global audience with Winter Games New Zealand carrying out a diverse event yet again. Winter Olympic, Paralympic and X Games stars are heading to New Zealand’s Southern Alps once again for the first major winter sports championships of the season. They compete for glory in varied sports such as freestyle skiing, snowboarding, alpine skiing, cross-country skiing and curling. The Winter Games New Zealand are one of the world’s top five winter sports competitions and the only one in the southern hemisphere. They are also New Zealand’s largest recurring sports event. It’s a uniquely Kiwi experience that athletes, coaches, judges and spectators all rave about. The relaxed atmosphere, friendly people, sporting action and festival fun with live acts and DJs – host towns Queenstown and Wanaka look forward to the biggest party on southern snow!

programme.title: Cape Epic 2019
programme.desc: The Absa Cape Epic is the world’s premier mountain bike stage race. The route changes every year, leading aspiring amateur and professional mountain bikers from around the world through roughly 700km of unspoilt scenery and 15 000m of accumulated climbing, over some of the most magnificent mountain passes in Western Cape in South Africa. The Absa Cape Epic is the most televised mountain bike stage race in the world and the only eight-day mountain bike stage race classed as hors catégorie by the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI). This official UCI status makes it a highlight on the professional racer’s calendar. The Absa Cape Epic also attracts aspiring amateur riders wanting to test themselves against the best. It is a full-service race, meaning that everything is taken care of from the start - all riders need to think about is riding.

programme.title: Andalucia Bike Race 2019
programme.desc: Gara andaluze e biçikletave është gara kryesore e biçikletave malore në Spanjë, e cila përbëhet nga gjashtë etapa dhe zgjat gjashtë ditë. Ritmi i garës nuk bie asnjë minutë gjatë këtyre gjashtë etapave. Në provën e fundit, çiklistët ngjiten në 1396 metra lartësi në mitikun Reventon dhe kalojnë përmes Trassierra-s, pastaj zbresin dhe përfundojnë në itinerarin e paharrueshëm Santo-Domingo. Një gabim në shtigjet shkëmbore do të thotë fundi i garës. Fituesit e edicionit të 9-të ishin spanjolli David Valero në garën e meshkujve dhe norvegjezja Hildegunn Hovdenak në atë të femrave.

programme.title: Music Voyager
programme.desc: Music Voyager is a music and travel broadcast series (television/cable, broadband, in-flight and mobile) that invites viewers to discover the exciting sounds of the planet. The host is Jacob Edgar, an explorer who does not search for lost cities or ancient ruins. He’s on the quest for a different kind of treasure…music. As an ethnomusicologist and world music record producer, Edgar travels the globe hunting for the best songs the world has to offer, and he suffers through some of the worst…so you don’t have to. Along the way, he’s rewarded with a backstage pass to concert halls, street festivals, recording studios and rehearsal rooms. With local musicians as his guide, Edgar tastes exotic and occasionally ghastly food, visits off-the-beaten path attractions and parties the night away to amazing concerts at hidden venues that only the locals know. Join music voyager for unexpected adventures and surprising discoveries that unveil the magic, mystery and music of far off lands.

The host is Jacob Edgar, an explorer who does not search for lost cities or ancient ruins. He’s on the quest for a different kind of treasure…music. As an ethnomusicologist and world music record producer, Edgar travels the globe hunting for the best songs the world has to offer, and he suffers through some of the worst…so you don’t have to. Along the way, he’s rewarded with a backstage pass to concert halls, street festivals, recording studios and rehearsal rooms. With local musicians as his guide, Edgar tastes exotic and occasionally ghastly food, visits off-the-beaten path attractions and parties the night away to amazing concerts at hidden venues that only the locals know. Join music voyager for unexpected adventures and surprising discoveries that unveil the magic, mystery and music of far off lands.

programme.title: The PAST Hunters
programme.desc: Derek Acorah’s The Past Hunters travel to Hoylake and investigate a building known as The Parade. Dating back to 1909, this once former school, still seems to have ghostly pupils and teachers taking class.

programme.title: The R.I.P. Files

programme.title: Desperate Hours
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore fire—a force both friend and foe. Mastered by humans hundreds of thousands of years ago, fire remains as inevitable as wind or rain, yet deadly when uncontrolled. Disasters can strike anywhere: from a Brussels department store to a Rhode Island nightclub where pyrotechnics killed 100 people. Firefighters still charge into danger, hauling hoses, scaling stairs with heavy tools, and lifting 35-foot ladders to save lives.

programme.title: The PAST Hunters
programme.desc: Derek Acorah’s The Past Hunters travel to Knutsford and investigate a former Crown Court. Multiple people have been sentenced to death and life in prison, but will the team encounter any of its former inmates tonight?

programme.title: The R.I.P. Files
programme.desc: The haunted Graffitti House dates from the Civil War and many of its previous residents still linger.

programme.title: Wild Australia with Ray Mears
programme.desc: Ray Mears explores the Great Barrier Reef starting on the Queensland mainland taking a boat out to Hervey Bay with whale expert Wally Franklin. They witness a mother hump back whale teaching her three month old calf the whale moves needed to survive the long migration to Antarctica.He flies out to Lady Elliot Island at the southernmost tip of the Great Barrier Reef where he goes scuba diving on the coral reef and discovers giant turtles and manta rays and shoals of big eyed trevelly fish.Back on the island Ray helps marine biologist Maggie O’Neal plant a Pisonia tree and finds out how the Pisonia trees kill the Black Noddy bird’s that nest in them in order to use their corpses as a fertile compost given the unforgiving ground of a coral island.

programme.title: Wild Australia with Ray Mears
programme.desc: Ray Mears journeys into the remote wilderness region of Arnhem land to the Cooper Creek Billabong. He’s there during the dry season and all the wild life is concentrated into a narrow stretch of water. He comes face to face with the dominant saltwater crocodile and watches as the croc manoeuvres a dead pig down river to a secret hiding place. Ray travels into Stone Country above the Billabong where he finds a gallery of ancient Aboriginal art and joins locals Connie Nayinggul and her grandson Moses on a fishing expedition. They catch a barramundi and cook the fish in a traditional ground oven using paper bark.

programme.title: Animal Embassy
programme.desc: Dali the emperor tamarin is mysteriously going bald—on his back! Keepers suspect two mischievous monkey roommates. Meanwhile, Kristina attempts an eye ultrasound on dolphin Ulysses, needing patience and precision. And it’s party time for Garoe the chimp, who celebrates his first birthday with a swinging cake surprise!

programme.title: Animal Embassy
programme.desc: As head of the aquarium, Ester sets a pace that’s hard to keep up with - especially on her Segway! And with a normal day including alligators, zebra sharks, jellyfish and shark pods - you may need a Segway to keep up with this Spanish dynamo too! When Loro Parque and their volunteers conduct one of their famous beach clean ups - you won’t believe what they unearth! Even better though, a turtle rescued last year with a fishing hook in its throat is being released back to its ocean home. Now that’s a good day at the beach.

programme.title: Meet My Wild Friends
programme.desc: Gasp at animal power, gawp at childhood innocence, this is the true story of children who live as friends with wild animals.

programme.desc: The European islands are renowned primarily for their hotel resorts. Why just lie on the beach when there is so much to see? Put on some good hiking shoes, pull your shoelaces tight, and get to know the entire island like the back of your hand.

programme.title: Wild Ones
programme.desc: The mighty grizzly bear. The tiny powerful ant. The lunging inimitable crocodile. The indestructible rhino beetle. The hammering mantis shrimp. Which is the strongest of them all? Grizzly Bear – North America’s sub-alpine lands are ruled by its mightiest resident. Ants – With 12,000+ species, ants are fierce, territorial defenders, dispatching intruders with ease. Crocodile – Ancient rulers of rivers, crocodiles have the strongest bite force ever recorded. Rhino Beetle – This forest dweller can lift 850 times its own weight. Mantis Shrimp – With bizarre eyes and a punch as strong as a .22 bullet, it’s a tiny powerhouse.

programme.title: Wild Ones
programme.desc: The explosive sprinting Cheetah. The mighty bounding kangaroo. The horned and leaping wildebeest. The powerful and sure footed horse. Or the quick footed pronghorn. Which is the fastest over land? Cheetah – On Africa’s savannahs, predator and prey race at breathtaking speeds. Pronghorn – North America’s fastest, it sustains 60 km/h and can reach nearly 100. Wildebeest – Iconic endurance runners; calves walk within minutes and run within days. Kangaroo – Australia’s largest marsupial, alert and powerful, built for speed. Brumby – Wild horses, symbols of strength and freedom, gallop unbridled across Australia.

programme.title: Ocean Odyssey: The Blue Realm
programme.desc: Whale Sharks: Gentle Giants introduces us to this amazing creature through scientists who are racing against time to save the species. Utilizing space-age technology from NASA and the Hubble Telescope, researchers are able to identify, catalogue and track individual sharks. In Mexico and remote Western Australia, whale shark tourism has proven to be both a blessing and a curse, as more and more boats vie for fewer animals. The program also features the remarkable story of shark cowboys who captured and transported 4 live whale sharks (in customized jumbo jets) to the Georgia Aquarium in Atlanta.

programme.title: Sarah Shark
programme.desc: Sarah travels to one of the top 10 dive destinations in Australia (Julian Rocks, Byron Bay, NSW) to dive with three species of Wobbegong Sharks within the Cape Byron Marine Park. She also conducts a street poll with members of the public to find out what they think about sharks.

programme.title: Race of Life
programme.desc: Predator vs. prey: this episode explores three bird escape tactics—climbing flight, horizontal speed, and diving. These behaviors reflect the evolutionary arms race. Birds of prey captivate us, from the mighty eagle soaring over open spaces to the peregrine falcon, the fastest animal alive. Vultures, often seen as omens, strip carcasses clean to survive. Whether elegant hunters or grim scavengers, each raptor plays its part in the Race of Life, adapting to stay one step ahead.

programme.title: Race of Life
programme.desc: Crocodiles, descended from reptiles 250 million years ago, lurk just beneath the waterline, striking fear into prey. Turtles, among the oldest reptiles, use their shells for protection and camouflage across land, freshwater, and sea. Snakes, from rattlesnakes to dwarf pipe snakes, share traits like legless bodies and lidless eyes, relying on sun for warmth. The king cobra’s venom can kill an elephant. Lizards escape predators by shedding tails, which regrow differently. For reptiles, cold blood offers a survival edge in the Race of Life.

programme.title: On the Cities’ Rooftops
programme.desc: How is life on the city’s roofs? This series scales new heights, exploring apartment buildings, towers and monuments to discover a world full of unsuspected treasures : our rooftops. By day and night, the population changes on these heights. There are people who work here, people who live here, and others who come here to relax. The world’s rooftops are a continual hive of activity.

programme.title: Udhëtimi i Ëndrrave
programme.desc: Shkurti 2017 na pa të niseshim për një udhëtim ekspeditë përmes Skocisë, Polonisë, Francës, Meksikës, Belizës, dhe kthimi. Jo vetëm që ishte aventura e parë jashtë Amerikës qëndrore, por ishte edhe hera e parë që i shtyva kufijtë e guximit tim për të bërë shumë gjëra që nuk i kisha bërë kurrë më parë. Mposhta frikën time të gjatë të zhytjes me skafandër dhe e zhytjes në qiell. Shkova në xhunglën Meksikane, provova ushqimin pikant të rrugës, u ngjita në piramidën Maja në mes të pyllit Belizan dhe i dhashë të hajë lule një gomari ekstravagant...

programme.title: Quirky Science
programme.desc: Plastic, once accidental, is now essential—from machines to daily items. It began with explosive billiard balls and beetle poop, leading to Bakelite and later nylon. Nylon’s popularity even sparked riots during WWII. But plastic’s durability and oil-based origin raise environmental concerns. Now, bioplastics grown in microorganisms—and possibly plants—offer quirky, sustainable alternatives for the future.

programme.title: Quirky Science
programme.desc: Rubber was first used by South American tribes for waterproofing and bouncing balls. Westerners struggled with melting rubber until Charles Goodyear discovered vulcanization, making rubber durable. This sparked the rubber boom, enriching cities like Manaus. Britain broke Brazil’s monopoly by smuggling seeds. Later, synthetic rubber and Kevlar were developed—Kevlar is so tough it can stop bullets. Rubber’s journey is full of quirky discoveries.

programme.title: Wow, I Never Knew That!
programme.desc: Learn the secrets behind thermos’ amazing technology! And they were the sweet candy pellets we loved as a kid, but did you know that Pez was created to help people stop smoking? And find out how a steamboat inspired Samuel Langhorne Clemens to change his name to Mark Twain!

programme.title: Wow, I Never Knew That!
programme.desc: It’s one of the world’s most famous train stations - Grand Central Terminal. We’ll take you on a trip to reveal its many fascinating secrets! And if they are cleaned without water, how do clothes get spotless when they are dry cleaned?

programme.title: Inside Outer Space
programme.desc: Come with us as we explore and unravel the mysteries of what lies beyond our planet Earth. This is a series packed with space stories and information about our universe covering what we can see, how we can live in space and what science tells us about the past and the future as we journey inside out of space.

programme.title: Inside Outer Space

This is a series packed with space stories and information about our universe covering what we can see, how we can live in space and what science tells us about the past and the future as we journey inside out of space.

programme.title: The New Frontier
programme.desc: The commercial space flight companies are edging closer and closer to flight readiness. Paying customers will soon be launching into space; tourists and their money is thought to be a major step forward into space and beyond. Blue Origin flight tests have been a great success and may launch commercial flights as soon as year’s end. Virgin Galactic is also smashing mile stones towards flight certification. SpaceX and its Manned Dragon capsule in direct competition with Boeings moves closer to an ISS taxi service.

programme.title: The New Frontier
programme.desc: The ESA - JAXA joint Bepi-Colombo Mission is moments away from launch. The target is Mercury which has been too long neglected; this mission will shed new light on this strange world of light and dark.

programme.title: Stolen Treasures
programme.desc: It’s the biggest museum in the world…the museum of artworks stolen over the centuries and never rediscovered. These works haunt the nightmares of their owners, and occupy the days of hundreds of police officers across the world, as well as those of a handful of private agencies; no country or museum of importance can claim to have been spared. According to Interpol, art theft is the fourth largest criminal trade, after the drug trade, the weapons trade and money laundering. How could it be otherwise, when the soaring price of art propels the value of some paintings into the tens of millions of Euros? This world appears to be full of mysteries. Crime syndicates rub shoulders with petty criminals and the police care more about recovering the items than they do about arresting the perpetrators.

programme.title: Wonder
programme.desc: Chromatic adaptation lets humans perceive consistent colors despite changing light. Some animals change color using chromatophores—for camouflage or signaling. Pink isn’t a real wavelength; our brains create it by blending light. Blue is rare in nature but appears through structural features in feathers and wings. Snow camouflage helps animals blend into winter landscapes using shades of white and gray.

programme.title: Wonder
programme.desc: The Monty Hall Problem shows switching choices boosts winning odds. The Birthday Problem reveals how just 23 people can have a 50% chance of shared birthdays due to multiple pairings. Gambler’s Ruin proves that in a fair game, the smaller bankroll loses over time. The Infinite Hotel Paradox explores the strange logic of infinity. The Locker Riddle uses factorization to reveal why only lockers with perfect square numbers stay open.

programme.title: Everyday elements
programme.desc: A series that puts chemistry in our everyday experience by showing the living connection we have with the chemicals and elements that make up our world. The matter that built skies and seas, the atoms that make up you and me, the chemistry around us that forms the things we touch, smell and see. This series shows us what the objects in our universe and in our homes are made from and why the particles around us behave as they do. Everything around us is built from Everyday Elements.

programme.title: Show Me Where You Live
programme.desc: Show me where you live is a documentary series that aims to answer the following question: How can human beings claim ownership to a space so that they can live safely within it, function as a society, and above all be in harmony with the environment around them? As we discover cultures and emblematic populations, we follow Philippe Simay who is at the heart of Inhabiting the World and represents its identity and originality. Philippe takes us on an epic adventure around the Human Habitat and sets the tone for the journey. As a humanist and philosopher, Philippe is a tireless surveyor of the city, and an explorer of living spaces. Determined to travel around the world, Philippe unveils how the populations that he encounters claim the space they occupy, shapes it and adjust to it.

programme.title: Wild Ones
programme.desc: Fanged Spiders with their scurrying bites. The Scorpion with its deadly sting... A sinister cold bloodied crocodile. The hypnotizing venomous snake. Or the King of Beasts, the Lion? Which one is the most dangerous? Lion – With golden fur and regal mane, the lion reigns as the ‘King of Beasts’. Scorpions – In scorched deserts, danger awakens after sunset. Spiders – Masters of webs and venom, spiders haunt myth and imagination. Snakes – Feared and revered, snakes symbolize power, death, and rebirth. Crocodile – Ancient and deadly, crocodiles inspire fear and legend across the globe.

programme.title: Wild Ones
programme.desc: The charming kangaroo. The cuddly koala. The beautiful Butterfly. The cheerful clown fish. Or the endearing budgerigar – which is the cutest of them all? Clownfish – Tropical oceans shimmer with dazzling marine life like the vibrant clownfish. Kangaroo – Australia’s countryside pulses with thousands of bounding kangaroos. Monarch Butterfly – Monarchs fill the skies, delicate and stunning in flight. Budgerigar – Social and lively, wild budgies flock in hundreds across Australia. Koala – Soft-furred and beloved, koalas are one of Australia’s most iconic animals.

programme.title: Ocean Odyssey: The Blue Realm
programme.desc: Sharks are BIG business in adrenaline eco-tourism. And some thrill seekers deliberately pursue close encounters with deadly sharks – without the protection of a cage. The bigger and more dangerous the shark, the better. Shark advocates Dr. Erich Ritter and Chuck Anderson have grave reservations about how far we are willing to go for a thrill. And they have intimate knowledge of the subject. Both men were brutally attacked by bull sharks. Shark Divers also examines the controversy surrounding a handful of high-profile attacks in 2008, including the first shark tourist killed while on a shark excursion.

programme.title: Sarah Shark
programme.desc: Sarah travels to one of the top 10 dive destinations in Australia (Julian Rocks, Byron Bay, NSW) to dive with three species of Wobbegong Sharks within the Cape Byron Marine Park. She also conducts a street poll with members of the public to find out what they think about sharks.

programme.title: Race of Life
programme.desc: Predators use speed, teeth, poison, and trickery to survive, but prey animals have evolved fascinating defenses. While fleeing is common, others use deception and chemistry—camouflage, mimicry, and toxins. Insects mimic leaves, snakes play dead, fish fly, and toads have poisonous skin. Predator-prey dynamics form an evolutionary arms race, with each side adapting to outsmart the other. Defense mechanisms include claws, poison, camouflage, and foul sprays. From zebra patterns to spider silk, strong defenses are vital to winning the Race of Life.

programme.title: Race of Life
programme.desc: Most sea creatures are predators, from tiny fish to giant squid. Built to hunt and survive, they’ve evolved into efficient underwater war machines. Stonefish lie in wait, disguised, while sharks, barracuda, and moray eels hunt with speed and precision. Reef fish must dodge lightning-fast barracuda and graceful but deadly moray eels. Lionfish use venomous spines, and stonefish can swallow prey whole. In the ocean’s depths, survival is a constant battle—an underwater jungle of razor teeth and stealthy ambushes.

programme.title: On the Cities’ Rooftops
programme.desc: How is life on the city’s roofs? This series scales new heights, exploring apartment buildings, towers and monuments to discover a world full of unsuspected treasures : our rooftops. By day and night, the population changes on these heights. There are people who work here, people who live here, and others who come here to relax. The world’s rooftops are a continual hive of activity.

programme.title: Udhëtimi i Ëndrrave
programme.desc: Shkurti 2017 na pa të niseshim për një udhëtim ekspeditë përmes Skocisë, Polonisë, Francës, Meksikës, Belizës, dhe kthimi. Jo vetëm që ishte aventura e parë jashtë Amerikës qëndrore, por ishte edhe hera e parë që i shtyva kufijtë e guximit tim për të bërë shumë gjëra që nuk i kisha bërë kurrë më parë. Mposhta frikën time të gjatë të zhytjes me skafandër dhe e zhytjes në qiell. Shkova në xhunglën Meksikane, provova ushqimin pikant të rrugës, u ngjita në piramidën Maja në mes të pyllit Belizan dhe i dhashë të hajë lule një gomari ekstravagant...

programme.title: Quirky Science
programme.desc: Canned food began with Napoleon’s contest to preserve food, won by Appert’s boiled, sealed bottles. The British later developed metal cans, though early ones exploded or caused illness. Can openers came 30 years later. Pasteur’s germ theory explained spoilage. Pressure-cooking improved taste, and now, ‘raddaperization’—zapping food—is the future. Canning evolved from battlefield necessity to high-tech preservation.

programme.title: Quirky Science
programme.desc: Medical history is full of odd cures—like bloodletting, which still helps in rare cases. Germs were once doubted until a doctor spotted bacteria between his teeth. Fleming later discovered antibiotics by accident. But now, ‘superbugs’ threaten this miracle cure. Refrigeration, once deadly due to toxic gases, evolved thanks to pressure-cooking and may soon use sound waves. From leeches to lab breakthroughs, medicine keeps evolving—what’s next?

programme.title: Wow, I Never Knew That!
programme.desc: It’s cheesy and and eaten all over the world! You’ll learn how Dominick’s pizza became Domino’s pizza. And we all know how going to a circus wouldn’t be complete without fluffy sweet cotton candy! We’ll explain how this feathery goodness Spun to life! And all the spy action heroes use them, but where did the term gadget really come from?

programme.title: Wow, I Never Knew That!
programme.desc: Take a trip to the Jersey Shore and learn how one of its famous boardwalks helped to inspire the iconic board game of Monopoly. And how did a donkey and an elephant become associated with politics? Plus, what’s the difference between top grain leather and full grain leather?

programme.title: Inside Outer Space
programme.desc: Come with us as we explore and unravel the mysteries of what lies beyond our planet Earth. This is a series packed with space stories and information about our universe covering what we can see, how we can live in space and what science tells us about the past and the future as we journey inside out of space.

programme.title: The New Frontier
programme.desc: The Japanese Asteroid sample return mission has reached its target and is surveying the space rock ready to dip down and take a sample. The return of asteroid material to Earth will aid scientists in the evolving asteroid planetary defense systems.

programme.title: The New Frontier
programme.desc: Two new space telescopes are in orbit and completing their shakedown; Gaia and TESS they too will be joined by the James Webb Telescope. Together they will be opening up a whole new vista into time and space.

programme.title: Stolen Treasures
programme.desc: It’s the biggest museum in the world…the museum of artworks stolen over the centuries and never rediscovered. These works haunt the nightmares of their owners, and occupy the days of hundreds of police officers across the world, as well as those of a handful of private agencies; no country or museum of importance can claim to have been spared. According to Interpol, art theft is the fourth largest criminal trade, after the drug trade, the weapons trade and money laundering. How could it be otherwise, when the soaring price of art propels the value of some paintings into the tens of millions of Euros? This world appears to be full of mysteries. Crime syndicates rub shoulders with petty criminals and the police care more about recovering the items than they do about arresting the perpetrators.

programme.title: Wonder
programme.desc: Carrion flowers like rafflesia arnoldii are rare, large, and foul-smelling, attracting flies for pollination. Aposematism uses bright colors to warn predators of toxicity, with some species mimicking these signals. Female cuckoos mimic predator calls to sneak eggs into host nests. Pheromones are chemical signals used for mating, tracking, or alarms. Deimatic behavior startles predators with sudden displays, helping prey escape

programme.title: Wonder
programme.desc: Saccadic eye masking helps the brain blur fast eye movements for clear vision. Plants move in response to stimuli for survival and reproduction. Language shapes how we perceive color—some cultures lack words for certain hues. Color blindness stems from faulty retinal cells and can be genetic or acquired. Perspective illusion uses geometry to create depth in art, a technique refined during the Renaissance.

programme.title: Everyday elements
programme.desc: A series that puts chemistry in our everyday experience by showing the living connection we have with the chemicals and elements that make up our world. The matter that built skies and seas, the atoms that make up you and me, the chemistry around us that forms the things we touch, smell and see. This series shows us what the objects in our universe and in our homes are made from and why the particles around us behave as they do. Everything around us is built from Everyday Elements.

programme.desc: Show me where you live is a documentary series that aims to answer the following question: How can human beings claim ownership to a space so that they can live safely within it, function as a society, and above all be in harmony with the environment around them? As we discover cultures and emblematic populations, we follow Philippe Simay who is at the heart of Inhabiting the World and represents its identity and originality. Philippe takes us on an epic adventure around the Human Habitat and sets the tone for the journey. As a humanist and philosopher, Philippe is a tireless surveyor of the city, and an explorer of living spaces. Determined to travel around the world, Philippe unveils how the populations that he encounters claim the space they occupy, shapes it and adjust to it.

programme.title: RV Explorers
programme.desc: RV Explorers, chasing 100 Sunsets. A TV show following a new motorhoming couple as they explore the towns and regions of NZ – experiencing various tourist attractions, events and joining in with other motorhomers to experience their favourite activities.

programme.title: Nomads
programme.desc: Pro mountain bikers test out their tricks in the dusty terrain of the Las Vegas dessert.

programme.title: Nomads
programme.desc: The Waiting is the hardest part. The anticipation of the next face shot, of an uncut heli run, and of an approaching storm is enough to drive this group of skiers to devote their entire lives to the pursuit of a sport and a lifestyle.

programme.title: Music Voyager
programme.desc: Music Voyager is a music and travel broadcast series (television/cable, broadband, in-flight and mobile) that invites viewers to discover the exciting sounds of the planet. The host is Jacob Edgar, an explorer who does not search for lost cities or ancient ruins. He’s on the quest for a different kind of treasure…music. As an ethnomusicologist and world music record producer, Edgar travels the globe hunting for the best songs the world has to offer, and he suffers through some of the worst…so you don’t have to. Along the way, he’s rewarded with a backstage pass to concert halls, street festivals, recording studios and rehearsal rooms. With local musicians as his guide, Edgar tastes exotic and occasionally ghastly food, visits off-the-beaten path attractions and parties the night away to amazing concerts at hidden venues that only the locals know. Join music voyager for unexpected adventures and surprising discoveries that unveil the magic, mystery and music of far off lands.

programme.title: The R.I.P. Files
programme.desc: Their bodies have long turned to dust, but the spirits of the original owners who built Bellewood remain in charge and don’t mind chasing out tresspassers.

programme.title: Travel Thru History
programme.desc: We’re exploring the other side New York state in Buffalo and Niagara. We’ll take the oath of office like Teddy, at the Roosevelt inauguration site in Buffalo. Then, we’ll take a tour of the Frank Lloyd Wright Martin house and learn about America’s most celebrated architect. We get soaked on the Maid of the Mist at breathtaking Niagara Falls, and defend the walls at Fort Niagara.

programme.title: Travel Thru History
programme.desc: We’re shipping off to Belfast, Northern Ireland on today’s episode. First, we’ll gawk at the world’s biggest Titanic museum. Then, we’ll learn about the province’s complicated history at the Ulster Museum. Finally, we get thrown in the slammer at the very creepy, Crumlin Road Jail.

programme.title: Nature’s Force
programme.desc: A snapshot of Seasons, how they work together and keep the globe in balance. Droughts are explored in terms of how we can predict them, proof our lives from them and collect data because of them. Hurricanes are explained, their power revealed and the measures that are used to help us survive their impact. Thunderstorms have a few stages of development that roll out in a particular order.

programme.title: Nature’s Force
programme.desc: How are Rainbows formed and what’s their science? We look at the largest Hail ever recorded and explain why it comes in so many shapes and sizes. Global Warming is a big issue and topic, and we give a nutshell insight to its meaning and impact on many levels. Forecasting is key and crucial to living with nature and its weather, as it involves precision technologies and expertise. Typhoon Halyan is an example of one of the most devastating storms in recent history and its story illustrates the power and destruction that Typhoons can cause.

programme.title: Big Coast
programme.desc: Running Southbound outside on Central Coast with a big Tyee Chinook Release finish North of Milbanke Sound!

programme.title: Wild Australia with Ray Mears
programme.desc: Ray starts by hitching a lift on a research crane to get a bird’s eye view over the Rainforest; from there, he can see the geographical position responsible for this lush vegetation: mountain range in the west and the sea in the east. He then goes down to the ground, delving into the heart of the jungle, he comes across millennial trees, camouflage spiders and a miniature dinosaur, the Boyd’s Forest Dragon. He pursues his journey by travelling on a zipwire with wildlife expert, Justin McMahon. Together they observe life in the canopy. Meanwhile, Ray’s cameraman Martin Hayward Smith has been filming an animal that can only be found in this part of the world: the Bennett’s tree kangaroo, a cute marsupial that lives like a monkey.

programme.title: Sarah Shark
programme.desc: Sarah travels to one of the top 10 dive destinations in Australia (Julian Rocks, Byron Bay, NSW) to dive with three species of Wobbegong Sharks within the Cape Byron Marine Park. She also conducts a street poll with members of the public to find out what they think about sharks.

programme.title: Outta Town Adventures
programme.desc: Outta Town Adventures travels both near and far to discover the best advenures the destinations have to offer. Season 1 visits attractions from California to Rwanda, Switzerland, Iceland, Utah, Zambia, Mexico, The Grand Canyon, Georgia (the Eastern European one) Louisiana, Hawaii, Mauritius and Seychelles. This TV series is dedicated to presenting history, culture and geography in a fun and pisitive way. It encourages people to explore this beautiful world - something that starts with simply getting out of town!

programme.title: Journeys in India
programme.desc: Chennai, formerly known as Madras, can trace its roots back to a tiny fishing village. Bill explores the city’s growth under the British East India Company, with visits to Fort St. George and the Fort Museum. We then travel to the nearby Sao Tome Basilica, the church and burial site of St. Thomas the Apostle. In Pondicherry, French influences can still be felt in the tree-lined streets, colonial mansions and cafés. Its beautiful setting on the Bay of Bengal makes Pondicherry a delightful place to spend the day. We also visit the ancient port city of Mahabalipuram, where the landscape is dominated by carved-stone architecture. The final highlight of our tour is the Descent of Ganga, which is the world’s largest bas-relief carving.

programme.title: Journeys in India
programme.desc: There is no city in India that is more British than Calcutta. The former capital of British India, Calcutta has gardens, buildings and museums to prove it. Throw away any ideas you have of this giant city and discover the treasures it holds.

programme.title: Journeys In Africa
programme.desc: This ancient ruined city, lost to history, was one of the most powerful in the world during its prime. The architectural sophistication and sheer size will amaze. Then Journeys heads out to the deep ocean for some big game fishing. Will we land the big one or return empty handed?

programme.title: Journeys In Africa
programme.desc: One of the 7 Natural Wonders of the World, Victoria Falls is an amazing spectacle that straddles the Zambia/Zimbabwe border. The force of the water is so intense that the water bouncing back creates a rainforest. Remarkably, the wildlife in the area is as abundant as the water going over the falls.

programme.title: The New Frontier
programme.desc: Launching payloads into space is a very difficult task, historically rocket launches are the proverbial ’swords into ploughshares’ Missiles designed to carry atomic warheads now send satellites and probes into the solar system. Ironically it’s one of the few exploits Mankind undertakes that doesn’t occur in nature.

And that’s all thanks to the Zamboni® Ice Resurfacing Machine. You’ll learn how and why it was invented! And ever notice some pistachio nuts are red in color? We’ll throw up the red flag and explain why the color is simply a cover up!

programme.title: Wow, I Never Knew That!
programme.desc: If you ever go camping there is one thing you do not want to leave home without, the swiss army knife! We’ll explain how it evolved into the most famous knife in the world and how the company’s name got “Cut” together! And where did the term ”cup of Joe” come from as well as the word java? And we all love a juicy hamburger, so where did these chopped meat patties come from?

programme.desc: Water: H2O Stories is a 3x52 series revisiting the story of water on planet Earth and its disrupted course over time which has led to the 21st century biggest challenge.

This series shows us what the objects in our universe and in our homes are made from and why the particles around us behave as they do. Everything around us is built from Everyday Elements.

programme.title: Quirky Science
programme.desc: Plastic, once accidental, is now essential—from machines to daily items. It began with explosive billiard balls and beetle poop, leading to Bakelite and later nylon. Nylon’s popularity even sparked riots during WWII. But plastic’s durability and oil-based origin raise environmental concerns. Now, bioplastics grown in microorganisms—and possibly plants—offer quirky, sustainable alternatives for the future.

programme.title: Inside Outer Space
programme.desc: Come with us as we explore and unravel the mysteries of what lies beyond our planet Earth. This is a series packed with space stories and information about our universe covering what we can see, how we can live in space and what science tells us about the past and the future as we journey inside out of space.

programme.title: Infestation
programme.desc: Forests are crucial for our survival on Earth. They absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and supply all living forms with clean oxygen. “We are like a patient in a hospital bed that is turning down their oxygen tank and thinking they could live with a little bit less oxygen and meanwhile the CO2 is increasing in the room” says journalist Andrew Nikiforuk.

programme.title: Music Voyager
programme.desc: Music Voyager is a music and travel broadcast series (television/cable, broadband, in-flight and mobile) that invites viewers to discover the exciting sounds of the planet. The host is Jacob Edgar, an explorer who does not search for lost cities or ancient ruins. He’s on the quest for a different kind of treasure…music. As an ethnomusicologist and world music record producer, Edgar travels the globe hunting for the best songs the world has to offer, and he suffers through some of the worst…so you don’t have to. Along the way, he’s rewarded with a backstage pass to concert halls, street festivals, recording studios and rehearsal rooms. With local musicians as his guide, Edgar tastes exotic and occasionally ghastly food, visits off-the-beaten path attractions and parties the night away to amazing concerts at hidden venues that only the locals know. Join music voyager for unexpected adventures and surprising discoveries that unveil the magic, mystery and music of far off lands.

programme.title: Desperate Hours
programme.desc: In this episode, we face the wild winds—hurricanes, cyclones, tornadoes, twisters, and typhoons. These powerful storms differ in form: hurricanes grow over warm oceans and can span 600 miles, while tornadoes are spinning air tubes touching ground and clouds, reaching speeds of 200 mph. They can destroy buildings, uproot trees, and hurl vehicles like toys. A tornado’s path may stretch over a mile wide and 50 miles long. The U.S. sees about 1,000 tornadoes yearly—2% violent enough to wreak havoc.

programme.title: RV Explorers
programme.desc: RV Explorers, chasing 100 Sunsets. A TV show following a new motorhoming couple as they explore the towns and regions of NZ – experiencing various tourist attractions, events and joining in with other motorhomers to experience their favourite activities.

programme.title: The PAST Hunters
programme.desc: Derek Acorah’s The Past Hunters travel to Stockport and investigate an abandoned Mil, Weir Mill, said to the most haunted Mill in the UK. Demonic figures haunt anyone that enters. Will the team survive the night with the spirits?

programme.title: The R.I.P. Files
programme.desc: Team members Patricia Marin and Malinka Franklin help a lost soul cross over into the light.

programme.title: Travel Thru History
programme.desc: We travel to the end of the rainbow in Dublin, Ireland. We’ll gawk at the Book of Kells, a holy book displayed at Trinity College. We visited the hallowed halls of St. Patrick’s Cathedral, and touched famed Irishman, Daniel O’Connell’s crypt at Glasnevin Cemetery. Finally, we learn the complicated history of Irish independence at Kilmainham jail.

programme.title: Travel Thru History
programme.desc: Get your sun tan lotion on, because we’re headed to the land of perfect weather and sunsets. We’ll sample a fish taco, climb the 100’s of steps of the California Tower, stand on the flight deck of the USS Midway, as well as, revisit San Diego’s founding on the San Salvador at the San Diego Maritime museum.

programme.title: Nature’s Force
programme.desc: What is La Nina and how is it being monitored? Find out the effects and the reach that this system is influencing. How did Indian Summer get its name and what is the science behind the phenomenon? Winter is the season that has the biggest effect on the planet, animal behaviour and often brings out the worst that nature can bring. Nature’s Halo is a magical sight with a scientific explanation. The story of and lessons from Hurricane Katrina give us a great understanding of the ferocity and speed that nature can unleash

programme.title: Nature’s Force
programme.desc: Weather is universal and it’s also Extra Terrestrial. Learn about space weather and how it can impact us on earth. Supercells are unique storms that scientists have learnt to measure into three types. Under the earth’s crust, nature is extremely energetic, and we see this through the Volcano which acts as our eye into the forces beneath our feet. Learn about the purple buzzing glow called St Elmo’s Fire, how it was named and were to look for it.

programme.title: Big Coast
programme.desc: Trolling cut plug herring from home base on Denny Island, BC!

programme.title: Wild Australia with Ray Mears
programme.desc: Ray takes the Great Ocean Road along the Antarctic facing coast of Australia – the longest South facing coastline in the world. He starts in Port Philp Bay the entrance to Melbourne Harbour where for the first time he sees a strange marine creature – the weedy sea dragon – a relative of the sea horse. He also swims with a unique species of dolphin – the Burrunan Dolphins.Crossing the Bay he heads off down the longest War Memorial in the world – the Great Ocean Road and meets 93 year old Doug Stirling who remembers the world war 1 veterans building the road.Ray visits the Penguin Colony on Middle Island where guard dogs protect the penguins from foxes and he watches the night time return of the penguins after a day spent at sea fishing.He takes to the seas and discovers the creatures of the deep waters – albatross, balls of krill and a pod of fast moving common dolphins.

programme.title: Sarah Shark
programme.desc: Sarah travels to one of the top 10 dive destinations in Australia (Julian Rocks, Byron Bay, NSW) to dive with three species of Wobbegong Sharks within the Cape Byron Marine Park. She also conducts a street poll with members of the public to find out what they think about sharks.

programme.title: Outta Town Adventures

programme.title: Show Me Where You Live
programme.desc: Show me where you live is a documentary series that aims to answer the following question: How can human beings claim ownership to a space so that they can live safely within it, function as a society, and above all be in harmony with the environment around them? As we discover cultures and emblematic populations, we follow Philippe Simay who is at the heart of Inhabiting the World and represents its identity and originality. Philippe takes us on an epic adventure around the Human Habitat and sets the tone for the journey. As a humanist and philosopher, Philippe is a tireless surveyor of the city, and an explorer of living spaces. Determined to travel around the world, Philippe unveils how the populations that he encounters claim the space they occupy, shapes it and adjust to it.
